boards.title: Your First Weekend at Franciscan University of Steubenville, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A campus-centered first-weekend sequence, followed by two daylight Steubenville stops with documented public-facing activities.

cards.title: Start at Christ the King Chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · campus
cards.notes: Use the chapel plaza as a clear meeting point, then check Chapel Ministries’ current schedule before attending Mass or prayer.
cards.short_summary: A central campus chapel and scheduled worship site.
cards.evidence_claim: Franciscan’s orientation schedule lists campus tours from Christ the King Chapel Plaza and a Saturday vigil Mass at Christ the King Chapel.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Chapel Ministries schedule for service times and any access changes.

cards.title: Have your first campus dinner
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Antonian Hall
cards.notes: Meet your new neighbors for dinner in the dining hall; confirm your meal-plan or guest-pass access before you go.
cards.short_summary: The campus dining hall appears repeatedly on the new-student schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Franciscan’s 2026 orientation schedule places Friday dinner, Saturday meals, and Sunday brunch in Antonian Hall.
cards.access_notes: Dining access may require an ID, meal plan, guest pass, or payment; verify with campus dining.

cards.title: Catch a Fieldhouse welcome event
cards.subtitle: Friday night · Finnegan Fieldhouse
cards.notes: Check the student calendar for a scheduled program, then use the Fieldhouse as the next shared stop after dinner.
cards.short_summary: A large campus venue used for orientation and faith-life programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Franciscan’s orientation schedule lists its Grand Opening in Finnegan Fieldhouse, and Chapel Ministries lists Festivals of Praise there.
cards.access_notes: Attendance and entry depend on the specific scheduled event; check the current student calendar.

cards.title: Make a plan at the J.C.
cards.subtitle: Friday night · J.C. Williams Center
cards.notes: Use the student center to reconnect with your group and look for the weekend’s posted campus activities before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A student-center stop that hosts orientation social programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Franciscan identifies the J.C. Williams Center as the student center, and its 2026 orientation schedule places a new-student dance there.
cards.source_title: Where Will You Be on Campus?
cards.access_notes: Building access and event entry vary; consult Student Life or the posted event details.

cards.title: Set up a library study stop
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · campus
cards.notes: Find the quiet areas, computer lab, and group rooms now, then bookmark the library site for its current hours and services.
cards.short_summary: A two-floor academic hub with individual and group study options.
cards.evidence_claim: The St. John Paul II Library says its building has quiet study areas, a computer lab, and group study rooms across two floors.
cards.source_title: About the St. John Paul II Library
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours page and room policies before visiting.

cards.title: Take a quiet Portiuncula pause
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · opposite Christ the King Chapel
cards.notes: Walk to the small stone chapel for quiet individual prayer or reflection; keep voices low and check bulletin exceptions first.
cards.short_summary: A replica chapel on campus dedicated to quiet prayer and adoration.
cards.evidence_claim: Chapel Ministries describes the Portiuncula as a campus recreation of the original and says it is mainly reserved for quiet prayer and adoration.
cards.access_notes: The page states daily 8 a.m.–8 p.m. access except when school-year perpetual adoration is active; check the Chapel Bulletin for exceptions.

cards.title: Walk the hillside Stations
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · behind the Portiuncula
cards.notes: Use daylight and sturdy shoes for the hillside path; move at a reflective pace and leave time to view the full sequence.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor, hillside devotional walk with 15 stations.
cards.evidence_claim: Chapel Ministries locates the outdoor Stations behind the Portiuncula and describes a hillside path with 14 stations plus a 15th at the top.
cards.source_title: The Stations of the Cross | Chapel Ministries
cards.access_notes: Use the path only in suitable weather and daylight; this is an outdoor hillside route.

cards.title: Check for an Anathan Theatre showcase
cards.subtitle: Saturday or Sunday · Egan Hall
cards.notes: See whether the theatre program has a public showcase on the calendar, and confirm the performance time and entry details before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A named Egan Hall performance venue used in orientation programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Franciscan’s 2026 orientation schedule lists the FUS Theatre Program Showcase: The Actor Games at Anathan Theatre in Egan Hall.
cards.access_notes: This card depends on a scheduled performance; verify the current theatre calendar and any ticket requirement.

cards.title: Take a daylight mural walk downtown
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · downtown Steubenville
cards.notes: Pick up a map or route advice at the Visitor Center, then photograph murals from public sidewalks while allowing time for the return trip.
cards.short_summary: A self-directed downtown art and local-history activity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Steubenville Visitor Center says the city has 24 larger-than-life murals on downtown buildings and provides maps and information for self-guided tours.
cards.source_title: Build Your Own Itinerary | Steubenville Visitor Center
cards.access_notes: The Visitor Center is at 120 South 3rd Street and publishes seasonal hours; use public sidewalks and observe traffic conditions.

cards.title: Finish at Historic Fort Steuben
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 120 South 3rd Street
cards.notes: If the fort is in season, take its daytime tour; otherwise stop at the Visitor Center for exhibits, maps, and local context.
cards.short_summary: A reconstructed frontier fort beside Steubenville’s Visitor Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Fort Steuben states that the reconstructed fort is open for tours May 1–October 31 and that the Visitor Center is open year-round on weekdays except holidays.
cards.access_notes: The site lists fort tours May–October and varying Visitor Center hours; confirm the current schedule before traveling downtown.
